rows.read: The October hike got talked back down: Bowman's 'I don't feel any urgency for taking further action at this point' and Daly (hikes likely, but not urgent for October) knocked October 27–28 from the post-CPI ~49% coin flip to ~31.6%; December ~90–94% (Citi flipped: 25bp in Dec, then hold, no cuts until June 2027). Yields faded — 2Y 4.80%, 10Y to a 3-week low of 5.1267%. PPI Thursday 7:30am CT is the next verdict; Warsh speaks Thursday night; blackout from Sat Oct 17.

rows.title: Policy divergence

rows.read: Split: the UK's growth leg covered the BoE — GDP +0.1% beat (vs -0.1%), 3m/3m +0.7%, industrial production +0.8%; Australia's went the other way — jobs -39.3K (vs +20K), unemployment to a five-year high of 4.7%. Japan split too: machinery orders +5.2% beat vs industrial output revised deeper to -2.4%. PPI + retail + claims Thursday 7:30am CT is the US verdict.

rows.title: Growth differentials

rows.read: PPI Thursday 7:30am CT (fcst 0.6% m/m, core 0.3%) is the next verdict on the broadening — September CPI's core beat twice (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y). Pipeline: German WPI +8.7% y/y (hottest since Feb 2023); the Beige Book had oil 'permeating all District reports.' What matters is what the bank does about it: October just got pushed back toward a hold.

rows.title: Inflation

rows.read: A genuine risk-off night — Nasdaq -1.9% (third straight down day), Kospi -7.7%, Nikkei -4.8%, VIX at a two-week high, silver -6.1% — and the haven bid still couldn't find a currency: the franc and the yen both slept through it. Fear keeps expressing through crude, not FX; the dollar traded the rate repricing, which faded.

rows.read: Brent ~$104.5 (-1.3%), WTI ~$94.1 (-1.0%), spread ~$10.5 — Washington weighing shadow-fleet sanctions-easing leaked the premium; the API's -11.1M-barrel draw was ignored (buyers won't chase $104+). EIA's official report Thursday 11am CT. Gold bounced to ~$4,135–4,144 (+0.8%) as the rate leg eased.

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities

rows.read: Wednesday's verified COT (Oct 6 cut): DXY net long only +12,011 — modest, not crowded. The crowd is in EUR/AUD/GBP shorts (-99,332 / -98,588 / -97,611; EUR ~1st and AUD ~2nd percentile) — squeeze-loaded against any dovish surprise. Contrarian rule unchanged: stretched longs = unwind risk, stretched shorts = squeeze potential. Next COT Friday.
